title: Stamp Size Photo Maker: 2 x 2.5 cm in Pixels, Free
description: Make a stamp size photo online: commonly 2.0 × 2.5 cm, which is 157 × 197 px at 200 DPI or 236 × 295 px at 300 DPI. Add a KB limit. Never uploaded.
intro: A stamp size photo is the small portrait some forms, affidavits and ID cards ask for. The common size, 2.0 × 2.5 cm, is preset; adjust it if your form says otherwise.

steps.name: Pick a photo
steps.text: Choose a clear front-facing picture. In such a small print the face must fill the frame, so crop close.

steps.name: Check the size
steps.text: 2.0 × 2.5 cm is filled in. If your form gives a different stamp size, type it in the cm fields.

steps.name: Pick a DPI
steps.text: Use 300 DPI for printing; 200 DPI is fine for uploads.

steps.name: Download
steps.text: Add a KB limit if needed, then save the JPG.

faq.q: What is the stamp size photo size in cm?
faq.a: It is commonly 2.0 cm wide and 2.5 cm tall. No single official definition exists, and some studios cut a little larger, such as 2.5 × 3 cm, so use the size your form names if it gives one.

faq.q: How many pixels is a stamp size photo?
faq.a: At 2.0 × 2.5 cm it is 157 × 197 px at 200 DPI and 236 × 295 px at 300 DPI.

faq.q: Can I print many stamp photos on one sheet?
faq.a: Yes. The photo sheet tool has a stamp option and places many copies on A4 or 4 × 6 inch paper with cut lines. Its stamp option is 25 × 30 mm, slightly larger than 2.0 × 2.5 cm.

faq.q: Will a stamp photo be blurry?
faq.a: Not if you start from a normal phone photo; shrinking keeps details sharp. Enlarging an already tiny image, such as one cropped from a group picture or a WhatsApp forward, is what causes blur.

sections.h2: Where stamp size photos are used
paras: Stamp photos turn up on paper forms with a small photo box, affidavits, some office ID cards and older application formats. Because the box is small, a full passport-size photo would not fit, and a shrunken one shows too much background. A tight crop where the face takes most of the 2.0 × 2.5 cm area looks best.
Online exam portals rarely say "stamp size"; they give pixels and KB instead. If your portal does that, use your exam kit or the custom size tool so both the pixels and the KB range are checked.
If your form writes the size another way, these are the same photo:
